title: A pull request's own review comment claims a milestone shipped that's still open
author: off-by-one
description: Extracts every 'milestone #N' claim phrase (milestone_claims.py's shared grammar, reused verbatim) from a pull request's own inline code review comment and checks the named milestone's real state. A milestone that exists but is still open is the seam: the reviewer's own permanent inline text claims a bundle of work shipped that, in fact, never closed out. The third and final review-comment-side leg of the claims-X grid, alongside review-comment-claims-unfixed-issue and review-comment-claims-unmerged-pr -- the six-sources-times-three-claim-types grid closes complete the moment this recipe merges.
confidence_notes: Age-gated off the review comment's own updated_at, mirroring review-comment-claims-unfixed-issue's and review-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's own reasoning (0.55 within 24h since last update, 0.85 past it) rather than tweet-claims-open-milestone's/release-claims-open-milestone's 0.5/0.85 bar -- a review comment is a text surface its own author can edit at any time, unlike a tweet or a mention, which is posted once and stands, so the same editable-surface grace window applies here that already applies to every review-comment-side claims-X leg. A claimed milestone that doesn't exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- that broken reference is a dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's. A claimed milestone that IS closed is excluded at confidence 0.0 too -- the claim was simply true. A review comment with no 'milestone #N' claim phrase at all, or no body at all, produces no surfaced candidate -- there is no claim to have broken.
